sources.entry: pymupdf - A fast MuPDF-based library for extracting, rendering, and editing PDFs and other documents.

summary.one_liner: PyMuPDF is a Python library built on the MuPDF C engine for extracting text, tables, and images from, rendering, and editing PDFs and other document formats.
summary.what_it_does: The library opens PDF, XPS, EPUB, CBZ, MOBI, FB2, SVG, TXT, MD and image files, and extracts plain text, rich dict output with font/size/color/bounding boxes, HTML, and XML. It detects and exports tables via find_tables() as Markdown or pandas DataFrames, and renders pages to PNG/JPEG or Pixmap data. It can add, read, and apply annotations and redactions, fill AcroForm fields, merge and split documents, and read or write metadata, bookmarks, and encryption. It also produces Markdown, JSON, and text output aimed at LLM and RAG pipelines, and offers OCR through Tesseract or RapidOCR. Office format support (DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, HWP, and others) is a separate, license-gated add-on called PyMuPDF Office.
use_cases: extract text and layout from PDFs
extract tables from PDF into pandas or Markdown
convert PDFs to Markdown for an LLM or RAG pipeline
redact or highlight text in PDFs
merge, split, or watermark PDF files
notable: Built on MuPDF, with both low-level page/text control and high-level convenience APIs
Structured output with bounding boxes, fonts, and reading order, plus native Markdown and JSON export for LLM use
Runs fully locally with no network calls after installation, per the README
Table detection via find_tables() with Markdown and DataFrame export
Redaction is a two-step process: mark, then apply, which permanently removes content
caveats: Dual-licensed: GNU AGPL v3 for open source, with commercial licenses from Artifex for proprietary use
PyMuPDF Office requires a license key; without one only the first 3 pages are accessible and functionality expires after an evaluation period
Does not support multithreaded use; the README recommends multiprocessing instead
Scanned PDFs need OCR, and the README notes Tesseract needs tessdata set up unless RapidOCR is used
